cells.tense: Right now you're carrying real weight, and you're carrying it on your own supply — not borrowing strength from anyone, not performing it for a room.
cells.ask: Let the strength you've built step forward and meet one thing openly, so what you've been holding can also be seen.
cells.core:
Nothing's been decided yet about which way this goes, and this is the part of you that stands easy in that. You can hold weight without knowing where it's headed, and it doesn't shake you. A strong body doesn't wait to be told what it's for before it's strong — it just is.

What you're carrying right now, you're carrying straight, and the store of it is bigger than the day is asking for. There's a moment here to let the holding turn into something you can stand in front of someone with, rather than something you keep behind your own ribs. The strength you built is done enough to show, and showing it doesn't spend it — it lets it land somewhere other than your own shoulders.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the weight on your own strength, and it's holding.
cells.verb: holding through material pressure on your own resources, unobserved

cells.tense: You're bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived, already sure you'll have to carry it alone, already spending against it.
cells.ask: Take one thing back to the person it belongs to — let what you give and what you get come out even for a day.
cells.core:
Nothing's been chosen yet, and you've already loaded yourself for every version of what might come — enough weight for all of them, and none of it real yet. You can hold; the trouble is you're holding everything at once. What's here is a muscle too ready, straining at a race nobody has called.

Real steadiness isn't the strain of pre-carrying. It's knowing what's yours, taking that, and letting the rest pass to whoever it actually belongs to. Letting one burden go back to its owner isn't dropping it — it's putting it where it can be carried and returned. The way back is what fair exchange does: one thing given back to its rightful hands, one thing received as yours to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying burdens that haven't shown up and might not be yours.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door you already walked through, waiting for it to open, when the room is behind you now.
cells.ask: Let one person out there know what you already gave — say what it cost, and let it be witnessed as done.
cells.core:
You don't feel strong right now, and that's not the truth — you're strong and it's gone quiet. You gave what you had to something that's now behind you, and you never got the acknowledgment that would let you feel the giving was real. So it sits there, unmeasured.

The strength is still in you; it just has nothing to push against because you're facing the wrong way. Tell someone what you carried, let them hear the whole of it, and the store you're sitting on can start to move forward again. That's not asking for praise. It's letting the weight you already carried be counted — and letting a finished thing be finished, in front of a witness.
cells.sheetLine: You gave what you had, and no one has told you it counted.

cells.tense: You're already holding the line through something hard, and you're calling it just getting through the day, not strength.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're still hoping for and keep walking toward it — let the persistence you already have get its light back.
cells.core:
You're doing something real right now, and you wouldn't call it that. You're showing up under pressure, staying with it, drawing on what's yours — and you've filed it under "this is just what's happening" instead of "this is me, doing this." The holding runs every day; the credit for it doesn't.

The persistence underneath didn't come from nowhere. Something is still pulling you forward, and if you turn and face it, the carrying gets lighter, not heavier. Hope isn't the opposite of strength here — it's what the strength has been running on the whole time. You don't have to be strong quietly forever.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the line and calling it nothing, but it's yours.
